answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on jobs or claim rewards. A registry ties votes to locked stake, caps each identity’s influence, and lets anyone prove double-voting to trigger a penalty. Splitting one stake among a falcon, a jetty, and an orchard of fake accounts does not multiply voting power; gaining more influence requires more capital at risk. The attacker therefore pays an opportunity cost and risks losing the stake if caught, though this does not stop wealthy attackers or collusion.
